title: prefill-decode-chunked-speculative-stage-overlap-kernel-scheduler-kv-cache-optimizations
author: Anika Rao
release_notes: Prefill/decode pipeline optimizations: chunked speculative prefill, stage overlap improvements, KV-cache and kernel scheduler tweaks yielding lower latency and higher throughput.
description: Context: Prefill/decode pipeline has allocation and scheduling inefficiencies when handling long prefixes and variable decode lengths. This PR implements chunked speculative prefill to split large prefill requests into smaller chunks, improves stage-overlap scheduling between prefill and decode to expose parallelism, and introduces kernel-scheduler heuristics and KV-cache eviction/lookup optimizations to reduce GPU idle time. Approach: 1) Chunked speculative prefill: split prefill into N-sized chunks, issue speculative decode for early tokens when later chunks pending; 2) Stage overlap: allow decode stage to begin processing chunks from prefill queue once initial KV cache segments are available, with correctness ensured by versioned KV segments and rebase logic; 3) Kernel scheduler: add short-term task prioritization to favor latency-critical small decode requests and coalesce contiguous KV-cache accesses; 4) KV-cache: avoid full cache materialization on host, introduce on-demand fetches and per-shard LRU with bounded prefetch. Testing: unit tests for KV correctness, new integration tests in perf-canary harness, end-to-end validation on internal benchmark lab. Results: p95 latency down 18-25% across evaluated models (redwood-1b to redwood-70b), 30% throughput increase under mixed request profiles, median latency unchanged or improved, memory overhead +2-5% with controlled evictions. Rollout: canary on dedicated pool (10%), monitor REDWOOD_PREFILL_DECODE metrics, ramp to 50% then 100% if no regressions over 24h. Backwards compatibility: falling back to prior pipeline when kernel-scheduler disabled; no API changes. Checklist: [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] perf benchmarks [x] docs updated [x] canary run planned. Related: ENG-1105, ENG-1023. See commits and files changed below.
commits: implement chunked speculative prefill and chunker pipeline (core logic and config)
add stage-overlap scheduler to allow decode-start on partially-available KV segments
kernel scheduler heuristics: priority lanes and coalescing contiguous kernel invocations
kv-cache: on-demand fetch and per-shard LRU with bounded prefetch; avoid full host materialization
add integration and perf tests, benchmark harness updates
fix race in kv-segment rebase and add additional correctness asserts
review_conversation: Jordan Kim: Nice work. Can you explain how rebase works if a speculative decode path is wrong?

Anika Rao: The chunker annotates speculative decodes with a dependency id; if a later chunk invalidates the prefix we mark affected speculative outputs and re-issue decode on the corrected cache. Added tests and metrics to detect these events.
Mateo Alvarez: Please add a metric to surface speculative rollbacks - we need alerting if rate > 1% of requests.
Anika Rao: Added REDWOOD_PREFILL_SPECULATIVE_ROLLBACK_RATE and dashboard panels in docs/perf.
Priya Shah: LGTM after addressing the race and adding integration test. Approved.
CI: All checks passed. Merge queued.
perf_summary: Observed improvements: p95 latency reduced 18-25% across redwood-1b to redwood-70b on mixed workloads, throughput increased ~30% under typical PLG traffic profile, GPU utilization up ~12%, memory overhead +2-5% with bounded evictions. Speculative rollback rate <0.4% in canary.
testing: Local unit and integration tests, perf bench runs in benchmark-lab, canary on dedicated pool with 10% traffic then ramp. Added deterministic tests for kv segment rebase, speculative rollback, and kernel-scheduler fairness.
rollout_plan: Canary 10% (24h) -> 50% (24h) -> 100% if no regressions. Monitor REDWOOD_PREFILL_DECODE_* metrics, REDWOOD_PREFILL_SPECULATIVE_ROLLBACK_RATE, p95 latency and error rate. Roll back by toggling PREFILL_DECODE_PIPELINE=v1 in config if regressions observed.
